Imagine wearing the outfit you designed and turning it into a one-of-a-kind filter. With Everywhere, the process is much easier and more fun than you might think. To explain it simply, we all know TikTok, right? It's the go-to platform for creating, sharing, and enjoying short-form videos. In this tutorial, we'll walk through the process of transforming garments created in Clo or Marvelous Designer into a TikTok AR filter using Everywhere, Photoshop, and Effect House. If you're new to Everywhere, we recommend checking out the basic tutorials first to get familiar with the fundamentals. We've included useful recommendations, and we've included useful recommendations, and we've included useful recommendations, and we've included useful recommendations, in the description. Be sure to take a look. Now, let's get started. Effect House Guidelines To create a TikTok AR filter, we need to use Effect House, TikTok's official AR development program. First, download and install the program from the link below. This tutorial is based on Effect House version 4.11.2. We've also prepared a manual and important guidelines for creating your own ar filters be sure to check the description for details when creating your filter in effect house make sure to follow these technical requirements we've also provided a template body mesh file for this effect house which is essential for designing outfits you can find the download link in the description so make sure to grab it by following these guidelines you'll be able to create a more stable and stunning ar filter now let's move on to the next step everywhere first we will create and dress the avatar using clo then we'll use everywhere for garment optimization rigging and bake map creation since everywhere works the same in both clo and marvelous designer feel free to use the software your most comfortable with downloading the outfit and importing the avatar the outfit used in this tutorial is provided by connect click the link in the card above to access connect add the garment to your cart complete the purchase and download the file import the downloaded file into clo or marvelous designer to begin working next you'll also need to import the body rig template fbx file for effect house simply drag and drop the file into your workspace when importing make sure to match the settings shown in the provided reference image fitting currently both the avatar and the outfit are positioned below the ground to correct this we first need to disable the ground collision setting right-click in the 3d window go to simulation properties and uncheck collision underground if you prefer a cleaner workspace you can use the 3d window to create a cleaner workspace if you prefer a cleaner workspace you can use the 3d window to create a cleaner workspace if you prefer a cleaner workspace you can also turn off the ground grid from the left menu in the 3d window once these settings are adjusted proceed with simulating the outfit onto the avatar modifying outfit details to achieve optimal performance we need to adjust the mesh type disable seam taping and modify the top stitch texture first to convert the entire mesh of the outfit to quad select all garments using control a then go to the property editor on the right panel and set mesh type to quad under geometry next disabling unnecessary seam taping can further optimize performance select all garments using control a go to the property editor find selected line and set seam taping to off additionally if the outfit has top stitch check its settings if the stitch type is set to obj it increases the mesh count which may negatively impact performance in this case switching top stitch to texture is recommended as it helps reduce the mesh count and improves overall efficiency now that the outfit is setting let's move on to the next step rigging once the outfit is fitted and all settings are finalized open everywhere by selecting everywhere under connect from the top to bottom of the outfit menu we will use the garment tab in everywhere to optimize the outfit apply masking and proceed with rigging polygon optimization first we will optimize the outfit the recommended FBX mesh count is 20,000 polygons or fewer to ensure smooth processing enter 15,000 in the input field next to garment and proceed with optimization once optimization is complete resimulate the outfit however if the mesh expands after simulation causing the outfit to clip into the avatar or behave unstably it may be best to skip resimulation evaluate the results and decide whether to keep the simulation based on stability masking next we will remove unnecessary mesh areas through the masking process activate the masking brush by clicking the brush icon next to the optimize button since AR filter outfits are designed in thin mode without thickness we will only apply masking to the front side of the garment now use the brush tool to select the mesh areas you want to remove if you need to unmask any part during the process switch the mode to subtract to restore the masked areas the masking brush can be used in both the 2d and 3d viewport so feel free to work in whichever view is more convenient for you rigging click apply in the rigging tab to proceed with auto rigging if weight adjustments are needed use the weight brush tools add subtract smooth to refine the rigging if the garment is penetrating the avatar or requires shape adjustments utilize the sculpt brush tools grab smooth fix intersection to clean up the surface and refine the shape once all modifications are complete click the exit button to close the brush window UV and baking once rigging is complete navigate to the material tab in the everywhere window to begin the texture process before proceeding with UV packing you need to set the image size you can choose from the available options but keep in mind that effect house supports the UV اليans which is very similar to 5D ones. but keep in mind that effect house supports the UV اليans which is very similar to 5D ones. but keep in mind that effect house supports the UV اليans which is very similar to 5D ones. supports a maximum resolution of 1024 by 1024 for this tutorial we will use the recommended resolution of 512 by 512 after setting the image size and seam size click the pack UVs button then adjust the desired settings and press the apply button to proceed with UV packing once the packing process is complete click the exit button to return to the material tab next we will proceed with texture baking before starting make sure that the ground collision setting is disabled right click in the 3d window simulation properties disable ground collision select the maps you want to generate then click the apply button for this tutorial we will use the default settings once the baking process is complete you will be able to see the generated normal map and ambient occlusion map once texture baking is complete the material list below will automatically generate materials corresponding to the number of UV tiles if you want to divide the materials for different parts of the garment and effect house you can separate and apply them accordingly for this tutorial we will proceed with a single material for the entire garment upload once all the work is completed click the apply button to proceed with the next step click the upload button to open the export options window since we are only exporting the garment make sure to deselect the avatar also as thickness is not needed select the thin option next select the entire texture and choose DirectX from the graphic library then click OK to upload to connect afterward access connect and download the uploaded FBX file when you open the downloaded zip file click the upload button to proceed with the next step click the upload button to proceed with the next step files you will find the generated FBX file along with the texture map files in effect house the MRAO map is provided as a PBR texture to convert the texture files received from Connect into an MRAO map we will use Photoshop first open Photoshop then select and drag adrop the ambient occlusion metalness and roughness maps into Photoshop and drag and drop the ambient occlusion metalness and roughness maps into Photoshop Photoshop to load them into separate tabs. The channel configuration for the MRAO map required by effect houses as follows. In this tutorial we will use the roughness map as the base and add the other maps accordingly. Select the roughness tab then press select all and copy. Move to the channel panel select the green channel and press ctrl V to paste. Click the ambient occlusion tab then press select all and copy. Return to the roughness tab select the blue channel and press ctrl V to paste. Select the metalness tab then press select all and copy. Return to the roughness tab select the red channel and press ctrl V to paste. Once the map creation is complete re-enable the RGB channels to make all channels visible. Then save the file in PNG format. Effect House. We will convert outfits created in Clo and Marvelous Designer into a lens for use on TikTok using effect house. First launch the installed effect house and type cloth in the search bar to open the clothing try on template. By default the template includes a sample avatar drive which is not needed. Delete this object from the hierarchy panel. Settings. Let's add lighting. Click the add object button in the hierarchy panel then select scene object environment light to set up the lighting. Next we will import the outfit and body fbx files. Click the plus button in the assets panel then select import from computer to bring in body rig template fbx and the fbx file of the outfit created in everywhere. Setting up an occluder box. To prevent the body from being visible through the outfit, we will set up an occluder body. Click the Add Object button in the Hierarchy panel and add Body Avatar Drive under AR Tracking. Once the Body Avatar Drive is created, drag the Body Rig Template FBX file from the Assets panel and drop it under Body Avatar Drive in the Hierarchy panel. Select Mesh Avatar 3D under Body Avatar Drive, then go to the Inspector panel and change Material 0 and Material 1 to Occluder Matte. Adding the Outfit Now, let's add the outfit using the same method we used for the occluder body. In the Hierarchy panel, click the Add Object button, then select Body Avatar Drive under AR Tracking. Drag and drop the Outfit FBX file under Body Avatar Drive. In the Hierarchy panel, drag and drop the Body Avatar Drive under Body Avatar Drive. In the Preview window on the right, check if the outfit is applied correctly. Applying the Outfit Textures Let's now apply the textures to the outfit. In the Assets panel, click the Plus button, then select Import from Computer to import the Diffuse, MRAO and Opacity maps. In the Assets panel, click on the Material 1001 applied to the Outfit Textures. In the Assets panel, click on the Material 1001 applied to the Outfit Textures. Then, in the Inspector panel, activate Texture On for the Albedo and apply the Diffuse Map. Similarly, check the Opacity box and apply the Imported Opacity map. Activate Texture on for the MRAO map and apply the Imported texture. If the texture is metallic, adjust the metallic value to get the desired effect. You can also adjust the Roughness value. The default is 0.5, but since the textures created in Clo and Marvelous Designer usually have higher roughness, we'll set it to 0.7. Now, check if the outfit model and textures are properly applied in Effect House, then proceed with any additional settings. Test Performance If the outfit moves correctly, click the Test Performance button at the top. It's important to check that the AR filter works properly on all devices before submitting. When the Test Performance window appears, click Run Test and wait for a moment. Did the result show passed? If so, click Done and let's proceed with submitting the filter. Preview on Device Before submitting the filter, you can preview it. Click Preview in TikTok at the top right and a QR code will be generated. Open the TikTok app. Go to Add Friend under Profile and scan the QR code. This will allow you to preview the AR filter you created. Make sure to check that the AR filter is working correctly. Create Icon To upload a thumbnail image, click the Create Icon button at the top right. When the window opens, select Upload Image. Select File to upload your own thumbnail image. Use the slider below the image to adjust its size and once you're satisfied with the settings, click the Done button. Submit Once all the work is complete, it's time to submit the AR filter. Click the Submit button at the top right. Set the effect name and other options, then click the Next button. After reviewing the information you entered, click Submit to complete the submission. The submitted AR filter will go through a review process and will be registered. Approval takes about 1-3 days. You can check the progress by clicking the avatar icon next to Submit, which will take you to the Analytics, Manage Effects page in Effect House. TikTok Is the filter's status changed to Active? If so, you're all done. Click on the filter and click Submit. Click on the filter in the Effect Name section to view the QR code. You can click Share or Save QR code to experience your filter in various environments. Thank you for participating in the tutorial. Got a fun idea? Try creating it as an AR filter and enjoy it. If you have any more questions or need help, feel free to ask in the Connect Community Board or through the comments. markdown_content: # Everywear to TikTok AR Tutorial (English/한국어) This document explains the step-by-step process of creating a custom AR outfit filter for TikTok using software tools including Clo or Marvelous Designer, Everywhere, Photoshop, and Effect House. It covers technical guidelines, garment preparation, rigging, texture baking, and final submission on TikTok. --- ## Introduction and Overview This tutorial guides users on transforming digital garments designed in Clo or Marvelous Designer into TikTok AR filters using Everywhere, Photoshop, and Effect House. It assumes familiarity with Everywhere basics and focuses on practical workflow steps to create and submit a unique AR outfit filter on TikTok. --- ## Effect House Setup and Guidelines Effect House is TikTok's official AR development platform, essential for creating TikTok AR filters. - **Version:** The tutorial uses Effect House version 4.11.2. - **Download:** Available via TikTok’s official Effect House site. - **Technical Requirements:** Follow the provided guidelines to ensure filter stability and performance. - **Template Body Mesh:** A body mesh FBX template file is provided for outfit design compatibility within Effect House. Download it before starting. - **Purpose:** Adhering to these guidelines ensures a stable and visually appealing AR filter. --- ## Preparing the Avatar and Outfit in Clo or Marvelous Designer This section details how to import, fit, and optimize garments for use in Everywhere and Effect House. ### Downloading and Importing Assets - **Outfit Source:** The outfit used is from Connect; purchase and download via the Connect platform. - **Import:** Load the outfit file into Clo or Marvelous Designer. - **Body Rig Template:** Import the Effect House body rig FBX file into the workspace for avatar rigging. ### Workspace Settings - Disable **ground collision** in simulation properties to correct avatar and outfit positioning. - Optionally, disable the ground grid for a cleaner 3D workspace view. ### Outfit Mesh Optimization - **Convert Mesh to Quad:** Select all garments, set mesh type to quad under geometry properties. - **Disable Seam Taping:** Turn off seam taping to reduce mesh complexity. - **Top Stitch Texture:** If top stitch type is set to OBJ (which increases mesh count), switch it to texture for better performance. --- ## Using Everywhere for Garment Optimization, Rigging, and Baking Everywhere optimizes garments for AR by reducing polygon count, applying rigging, and generating texture maps. ### Garment Optimization - Recommended polygon count: 20,000 or fewer; set target to 15,000 polygons. - After optimization, resimulate the outfit; if mesh instability or clipping occurs, consider skipping resimulation. ### Masking - Apply masking to remove unnecessary mesh areas, focusing on the front side as AR outfits are thin. - Use masking brush in 2D or 3D view. - Toggle between add and subtract modes to fine-tune masked areas. ### Rigging - Use the auto rigging feature via the rigging tab. - Refine weights with brush tools: add, subtract, smooth. - Adjust garment shape and fix mesh intersections with sculpt brushes: grab, smooth, fix intersection. - Exit brush tools after completing modifications. ### UV Packing and Texture Baking - Set image size (max 1024x1024 supported by Effect House); tutorial uses 512x512. - Click "Pack UVs", adjust settings, and apply. - Disable ground collision before baking textures. - Bake maps such as normal and ambient occlusion using default settings. - Materials auto-generate matching UV tiles; optionally separate materials for different garment parts. - Use a single material for simplicity in this tutorial. ### Export and Upload - Deselect avatar, select "thin" option for outfit thickness. - Use DirectX graphic library for texture format. - Upload garment to Connect, then download the FBX and texture files for Effect House import. --- ## Creating MRAO Maps in Photoshop Effect House requires MRAO (Metalness, Roughness, Ambient Occlusion) maps combined into a single texture with specific channel assignments. ### Procedure 1. Open ambient occlusion, metalness, and roughness maps in Photoshop. 2. Use the roughness map as the base. 3. Copy roughness map; paste into the green channel. 4. Copy ambient occlusion; paste into the blue channel. 5. Copy metalness; paste into the red channel. 6. Re-enable RGB channels and save as PNG. --- ## Effect House: Importing and Setting Up the AR Filter ### Template and Scene Setup - Open Effect House and load the **Clothing Try-On Template**. - Remove the default sample avatar drive object. ### Lighting - Add environment light via the hierarchy panel for proper scene illumination. ### Importing Assets - Import the body rig template FBX. - Import the optimized outfit FBX created with Everywhere. ### Occluder Setup - Add an occluder body to prevent the avatar body from showing through the outfit. - Add "Body Avatar Drive" under AR Tracking. - Assign the body rig template FBX under this object. - Set materials 0 and 1 to **Occluder Matte** to hide the avatar mesh beneath the outfit. ### Adding the Outfit - Add another "Body Avatar Drive" object under AR Tracking. - Drag the outfit FBX under this new Body Avatar Drive. - Nest this outfit Body Avatar Drive under the occluder Body Avatar Drive for correct hierarchy. - Verify correct outfit placement in the preview window. --- ## Applying Textures in Effect House ### Import Textures - Import Diffuse, MRAO, and Opacity maps into the assets panel. ### Material Configuration - Select the material applied to the outfit (e.g., Material 1001). - Enable and assign textures: - Albedo: Apply Diffuse map. - Opacity: Apply Opacity map and enable opacity. - MRAO: Apply the combined MRAO texture and enable it. ### Adjust Material Properties - Adjust metallic value if the texture appears metallic. - Set roughness value; default is 0.5, but 0.7 is recommended for Clo/Marvelous Designer textures. --- ## Testing and Previewing the AR Filter ### Test Performance - Use the "Test Performance" button to run a device compatibility check. - Confirm the test passes to ensure filter stability on multiple devices. ### Preview on Device - Generate a QR code via "Preview in TikTok". - Open TikTok app, scan QR under Add Friend > Profile to preview the AR filter directly on a device. --- ## Creating an Icon and Submitting the AR Filter ### Icon Creation - Use "Create Icon" button to upload a custom thumbnail image. - Adjust the image size with the slider and confirm. ### Submission Process - Click "Submit" and enter effect name and options. - Review information and confirm submission. - The filter goes through a 1-3 day review process. ### Post-Submission - Check submission status under Analytics > Manage Effects in Effect House. - Once status changes to "Active", the filter is live. - Access QR code for sharing or saving to test the filter in various environments. --- # Summary This tutorial provides detailed instructions for creating TikTok AR outfit filters starting from garment design in Clo or Marvelous Designer, through optimization and rigging in Everywhere, texture baking and MRAO map creation in Photoshop, to filter assembly and submission in Effect House. Following these steps ensures a high-quality, performant AR filter ready for TikTok’s platform.

chunks.content: - Nest this outfit Body Avatar Drive under the occluder Body Avatar Drive for correct hierarchy. - Verify correct outfit placement in the preview window. --- ## Applying Textures in Effect House ### Import Textures - Import Diffuse, MRAO, and Opacity maps into the assets panel. ### Material Configuration - Select the material applied to the outfit (e.g., Material 1001). - Enable and assign textures: - Albedo: Apply Diffuse map. - Opacity: Apply Opacity map and enable opacity. - MRAO: Apply the combined MRAO texture and enable it. ### Adjust Material Properties - Adjust metallic value if the texture appears metallic. - Set roughness value; default is 0.5, but 0.7 is recommended for Clo/Marvelous Designer textures. --- ## Testing and Previewing the AR Filter ### Test Performance - Use the "Test Performance" button to run a device compatibility check. - Confirm the test passes to ensure filter stability on multiple devices. ### Preview on Device - Generate a QR code via "Preview in TikTok". - Open TikTok app, scan QR under Add Friend > Profile to preview the AR filter directly on a device. --- ## Creating an Icon and Submitting the AR Filter ### Icon Creation - Use "Create Icon" button to upload a custom thumbnail image. - Adjust the image size with the slider and confirm. ### Submission Process - Click "Submit" and enter effect name and options. - Review information and confirm submission. - The filter goes through a 1-3 day review process. ### Post-Submission - Check submission status under Analytics > Manage Effects in Effect House. - Once status changes to "Active", the filter is live. - Access QR code for sharing or saving to test the filter in various environments. --- # Summary This tutorial provides detailed instructions for creating TikTok AR outfit filters starting from garment design in Clo or Marvelous Designer, through optimization and rigging in Everywhere, texture baking and MRAO map creation in Photoshop, to filter assembly and submission in Effect House. Following these steps ensures a high-quality, performant AR filter ready for TikTok’s platform.
